To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) scrapie infectivity is associated with a detergent-insoluble, high molecular weight complex that is sedimented through 20% to 40% Nyzodenz gradients; 2) the degree of aggregation of the scrapie complex is influenced by the conditions used for purification; 3) scrapie infectsivity is not destroyed during purification; and 4) the scrapie complex may contain more than one type of scrapie agent.
the scrapie agent is an infectious macromolecular complex that is insoluble in aqueous solutions and that is purified by equilibrium density gradient centrifugaton in Nycodens gradients.
the scrapie agent is an infectious macromolecular complex which can be isolated in high purity and which has a buoyant density of 1.18 g/ml.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of the scrapie-associated fibrils.
the physical and chemical properties of scrapie infectivity.
the isolation of the scrapie prion protein, the proteinaceous agent that causes scrapie.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of a suitable detergent, the scrapie agent is associated with a membrane component which is insoluble in Nycodenez.

the scrapie agent exists as a macomolecular complex, the infectivity of which is highly sensitive to the nature of the conditions under which the complex is measured and that the scrapie-associated fibrils are not the agent.
the scrapie agent is a macromolecular entity of high molecular weight, with a sedimentation coefficient of 200-300S.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scrapie agent is a proteinaceous infectious particle that is composed of a protein and an RNA molecule.
the scrapie agent is a complex of at least two different components, a proteinaceous component with a sedimentation coefficient of 7S to 10S and a lipid component.
the scrapie agent has a density of 1.18-1.21 g/cm3 and a sedimentation coefficient of 200 S.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scrapie agent is not a simple, homogeneous, macromolecular complex, but rather a complex of macromolecules, and that the scrapie infectivity assay is not quantitative.
the scrapie agent is a macromolecular aggregate that is highly sensitive to denaturing agents.
scrapie infective prions are found in a detergent-insoluble complex that sediments through 40% (w/w) Nycodenz and that they are highly aggregated in the presence of urea.
